status_summary: An executive order of 2025-01-23 (Sec. 5) bars executive agencies, unless required by law, from taking action to establish, issue or promote a central bank digital currency in the United States or abroad and directs that any ongoing plans be terminated. Congress completed passage of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644) on 2026-06-22 (Senate, 85 to 5) and 2026-06-23 (House, 358 to 32); it was presented on 2026-06-29 and became Public Law 119-101 without the President's signature on 2026-07-11. Its Title XI, Sec. 1101, codified at 12 U.S.C. 423, bars the Board of Governors and the Federal reserve banks from creating or issuing a CBDC, directly or through intermediaries, except for open, permissionless and private dollar-denominated currency, and ceases to be effective on 2030-12-31, so the statutory bar is time-limited. The House passed the broader H.R. 1919 on 2025-07-17 (219 to 210); no Senate action on it or its companion S. 1124 is recorded.

timeline.event: Executive order on digital financial technology prohibits agencies from establishing, issuing or promoting a CBDC and directs termination of any ongoing CBDC plans (Section 5); it also sets up a working group on digital asset markets.
House passed H.R. 1919, the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, prohibiting Federal Reserve Banks from issuing a CBDC and the Board from testing, studying or developing one (engrossed House text).

GENIUS Act (S. 1582) signed on 2025-07-18 (Public Law 119-27), creating a federal framework for payment stablecoins; the enrolled text on GovInfo does not mention a central bank digital currency, so it neither creates nor bars one.
The Senate concurs in the House amendment to H.R. 6644 (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act) with an amendment (SA 5823), 85 to 5 (Record Vote 182).

The House agrees to the Senate amendment to H.R. 6644, 358 to 32 (Roll no. 224), completing congressional passage of the bill, which includes a time-limited prohibition on the Federal Reserve issuing a CBDC.
H.R. 6644 is presented to the President.

The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644) becomes Public Law 119-101, dated 2026-07-11 in the law's header, without the President's signature (BILLSTATUS records that it was sent to the Archivist unsigned). Its Title XI, Sec. 1101 (Central bank digital currency), codified at 12 U.S.C. 423, bars the Board of Governors and the Federal reserve banks from creating or issuing a central bank digital currency or a substantially similar digital asset, directly or through a financial institution or other intermediary, excepts open, permissionless and private dollar-denominated currency, and ceases to be effective on 2030-12-31. The Block places the event on the prior Friday (2026-07-10).

uncertainties: The executive order (Sec. 5), the H.R. 6644 BILLSTATUS record and the House Financial Services Committee section-by-section were read on whitehouse.gov, govinfo.gov and financialservices.house.gov; the enrolled-law header, number, date and table of contents (Title XI, Sec. 1101) were read on govinfo.gov in an earlier pass. The operative text of Sec. 1101 was read on 2026-10-26 as codified at 12 U.S.C. 423 on the Cornell Legal Information Institute (source credit Pub. L. 119-101, title XI, sec. 1101, 140 Stat. 983): it covers the Board and the Federal reserve banks directly or indirectly through a financial institution or other intermediary, defines digital asset by reference to 12 U.S.C. 5901, excepts open, permissionless and private dollar-denominated currency, and ceases to be effective on 2030-12-31, so the Duke blog, law-firm analyses and committee summary are no longer the only basis for scope and sunset. The Statutes at Large text was not read, because the govinfo.gov law text is truncated before Title XI and congress.gov could not be opened in this review; the uscode.house.gov page for 12 U.S.C. 423, read on 2026-11-03, matches the Cornell text (source credit Pub. L. 119-101, title XI, sec. 1101, 140 Stat. 983; ceases to be effective 2030-12-31; rule of construction that nothing authorizes the Board to issue a CBDC without an Act of Congress). BILLSTATUS confirms the final vote order (Senate 2026-06-22, House 2026-06-23) and that the bill was sent to the Archivist unsigned on 2026-07-11, which replaces an earlier news-dated passage event and a trade report giving a day earlier. H.R. 1919 status rests on its BILLSTATUS record as read by the researcher. The GENIUS Act date (2025-07-18) and number (Public Law 119-27) are confirmed by a White House statement and by the enrolled law on GovInfo, whose full text was read and does not mention a central bank digital currency. The Board's CBDC page on federalreserve.gov (update date 2022-01-21) was re-opened on 2026-11-03 and states no decision on pursuing a CBDC without referring to the 2025 order or the 2026 law; a search restricted to federalreserve.gov found no Board statement on the statutory bar, so whether the Fed has formally ended CBDC research was not verified and no Fed decision is asserted in this record. The 2026-09-24 timeline event cites the Board's own press release on federalreserve.gov; that release concerns stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act and does not mention a central bank digital currency, so it is context and does not affect the stage. The chapter's other monetary options (free banking, commodity-backed money, a commission on alternatives to the Fed, limits on lender of last resort) were not researched.
